diffraction and absorption are troublesome for highfinesse filters.
absorption and diffraction losses in all-fiberoptic Fabry-Perots can be calculated with a rigorous modal three-dimensional method.
the three-dimensional modal method is a powerful tool to analyze the losses in all-fibre filters.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following points: (i) the absorption and diffraction losses of FP filters, (ii) the influence of the filter length on the diffraction losses, and (iii) the influence of filter thickness and refractive index on diffraction and absorption.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diffraction and the absorption losses in the filter are both important for high finesse and that both losses can be reduced by using low-loss and low-dispersion fiber materials.
, for high-fineses filters, the diffraction into cladding modes is more serious than the absorption losses, but for low-finesse filters the absorption losses are the main loss mechanism.
the FP filter is a very useful device for wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) systems, but the FP filter is not suitable as a wavelength discriminator for single-mode fiber communications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diffraction losses are the most important loss factor, and the absorption losses are the second important loss factor.
the absorption losses and diffractions are not negligible for all-fiber FP filters with a finesse higher than 10, and they should be taken into account in the filter design.
the diffraction into cladding modes is the main cause of the insertion losses in all-fibre multilayer filters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the absorption losses and diffractions can be reduced significantly by using a high-index core fiber and a low-index cladding fiber.
, to reduce absorption losses and diffractions in all-fiber filters, one should use fibers with small core diameters, large numerical apertures, and small mode-field diameters.
the diffraction loss can be minimized by using a short cavity length.
